A1.justification: Both PDFs describe B-cos LM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained experiments and analyses can be matched despite substantial reorganization and the added decoder-only study.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, explanation evaluations, a human study, ablations, and analyses of alignment pressure and bias.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds explainable-model comparisons and decoder-only language-modeling and explanation evaluations.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a generation variant for GPT-2 and Llama-3.2: the tied language head is excluded from B-cos conversion, standard cross-entropy replaces the classifier's BCE objective, and explanations contrast target and foil tokens (Section 7). These extend the training and explanation procedures; the original classification method remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds OpenWebText training and held-out language-modeling evaluation, nine BLiMP subsets testing linguistic phenomena, and Indirect Object Identification. This extends the evaluated coverage from sequence classification to next-token prediction and explanations of grammatical and object-identification decisions. AG News, IMDB, HateXplain, and Wikipedia pre-training are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds Saloss BERT/RoBERTa and RGFS-SA BERT comparisons, plus decoder comparisons involving Random, Grad Norm, IxG, Occlusion, Logit, and ALTI Logit. Logit and ALTI Logit scores are reproduced from cited work. Conversely, the broad post-hoc-on-B-cos comparison blocks in v1 Tables 2, 6, and 7 disappear; IxG remains in the component ablation.

E3.justification: The reported IMDB B setting changes from 1.5 to 1.25, including the training-strategy comparison. New decoder protocols use B=1.1, contrastive MRR, target–foil probability gaps, held-out perplexity, and PAD-token occlusion. Human-study instructions change from 50 examples, 25 per task, to 100 examples, 50 per task; unchanged ratings do not establish that additional data were collected.

E4.justification: The analysis of combining versus separating task fine-tuning and B-cos conversion is revised using B=1.25 and replacement results (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 5). The component ablation, B-sensitivity analysis, alignment analysis, and bias cases remain substantially unchanged. Moving the component ablation from v1 Appendix C to v2 Section 4.6 does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 drops the explicit three-run averaging statement from the component-ablation table, retained from v1 Table 5 as v2 Table 4. Three-run reporting elsewhere and the human study's Bonferroni-corrected paired t-tests remain. The new parenthesized ablation values are differences from the full system, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds Saloss, RGFS-SA, and decoder results while removing most post-hoc-on-B-cos scores and their cost measurements. Retained accuracies also change: conventional BERT on AG News is revised from 95.76% to 94.76% in Figure 2. IMDB B-cos BERT Comp changes from 75.33 to 74.18 under the revised B setting, so this is not a same-setting performance comparison. New results include B-cos GPT-2's BLiMP MRR of 0.7561.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit bias-free normalization formula and reasoning about running-mean centering in Section 3.2; most other component derivations move from v1 Appendix D. The rewritten composition Equation 6 also introduces an erroneous equality: its right-hand side omits the input X present on the left.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion add the claim of a first application to decoder-only models and generation tasks. This broadens the claimed contribution beyond v1's demonstrated encoder classification scope. Practical guidelines cease to be the fourth highlighted contribution but remain in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 removes the limitations concerning absent explainable-model comparisons and encoder-only evaluation, and adds a concrete limitation about token interactions and compositional semantics, including negation. It also discusses additional decoder training overhead. Existing interpretations concerning alignment, sparsity, and bias amplification remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents decoder corpus sizes, training epochs, learning rate, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and a 10,000-sentence perplexity set. It also adds Saloss implementation information and previously unstated encoder pre-training details, including 25,000 Wikipedia sentences and language-head treatment, and clarifies that CLS is not perturbed. Conversely, the project code-access link and participant-background and compensation disclosures disappear.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around generative explanations, different explanation formats, modern encoders, and LLMs. Added references include Ferrando et al. for generative attribution, Chrysostomou and Aletras for Saloss, and Saha et al. for rationale-guided models. The Brinner and Zarrieß citation accompanying v1's justification for omitting explainable-model comparisons is removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and expands methodological explanations. Separate human-evaluation, qualitative-analysis, and efficiency sections become subsections of Experiments; the component derivations and ablation move into the main text. The appendix organization and concluding sections are also revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, with figures and tables resized and repositioned throughout. Classification plots add Saloss bars, faithfulness and efficiency tables are restructured, and the ablation table gains colored differences. New tables present decoder evaluations, dataset examples, and the RGFS-SA comparison.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by adding Saloss and RGFS-SA comparisons, directly addressing v1's stated lack of comparisons with other explainable models, and by documenting and evaluating a decoder-only extension. These gains outweigh the loss of most same-model post-hoc comparisons and the project code link. Nevertheless, unexplained revisions to accuracies and human-study size, the removed ablation run-count statement, and the missing input factor in Equation 6 weaken reporting quality.
